lessons.title: Time units and durations
lessons.summary: Convert between seconds, minutes, hours and calendar units.
lessons.objective: Convert between seconds, minutes, hours and calendar units.
lessons.before: Recall how many minutes there are in one hour.
lessons.ideas:
Multiply the hours by 60 and add the extra minutes.

Keep the number of whole groups and the leftover seconds.

Use the given number of days in a month or read it from a calendar.
lessons.method:
How many minutes make up the duration?

Separate the complete hours from the leftover minutes. Count 60 minutes per hour.

What remains after whole minutes?

Group seconds in lots of 60. Each full group is one minute.

How are days, weeks, months and years related?

There are 7 days in a week and 12 months in a year. Use 365 days when the question treats a year as 365 days.
mistakes: The two parts of a duration are in different units.
The decimal digits of a number of minutes do not tell you the seconds.

examples.title: Convert a duration to minutes
examples.question: A school event lasts 3 h 7 min. Give its duration in minutes.
examples.solution:
Count 60 minutes for each of the 3 full hours, giving 180 minutes.

Add the extra 7 minutes.

The answer is \(187\).

examples.title: Use the remainder when converting seconds
examples.question: A clip lasts 306 seconds. After recording all full minutes, how many seconds are left?
examples.solution:
306 contains 5 whole groups of 60 seconds.

Subtract 300 seconds and keep the remainder.

The answer is \(6\).

examples.title: Count full years using the stated convention
examples.question: A plan runs for 1 years and 6 days. Use 365 days per year. Give the duration in days.
examples.solution:
Take 1 groups of 365 days.

Add 6 days to the 365 days.

The answer is \(371\).

lessons.title: 12-hour, 24-hour and analogue clocks
lessons.summary: Convert between clock systems and read the hour and minute hands.
lessons.objective: Convert between clock systems and read the hour and minute hands.
lessons.before: Recall how many minutes there are in one hour.
lessons.ideas:
Convert the hour using a.m. or p.m. Keep the minutes the same.

If the 24-hour hour is 13 or more, subtract 12. Read hour 00 as 12 a.m.

Read the hour just passed by the short hand. Count the long hand in fives. At the top the minutes are zero.
lessons.method:
What time is noon or midnight?

The 24-hour clock starts at 00:00. Noon is 12:00. Afternoon times after 12:59 have hour 13 or later.

When should I write a.m. or p.m.?

The 12-hour clock names the half-day. A time from noon onwards uses p.m.

Which hand tells me the minutes?

The long hand indicates minutes. It takes five minutes to move from one big number to the next.
mistakes: The hour for 12 a.m. becomes 00. The hour for 12 p.m. stays at 12.
Write both the digits and the a.m. or p.m. label.
At half past the hour the short hand is halfway to the next number.

examples.title: Convert a 12-hour reading to 24-hour time
examples.question: Write \(3:06\) a.m. in 24-hour notation.
examples.solution:
Keep this morning hour.

Keep the minutes at \(06\).

The time is \(03:06\).

examples.title: Convert a 24-hour reading to 12-hour time
examples.question: Write \(09:21\) in 12-hour notation.
examples.solution:
Hours below 12 are a.m. Hours from 12 onwards are p.m.

The 12-hour reading uses hour 9 with the same minutes.

The time is 9:21 a.m..

examples.title: Read the hour and minute hands
examples.question: It is morning. An analogue clock's minute hand points to 5. Its hour hand has passed 5 and has not reached 6. Write the time in 24-hour notation.
examples.solution:
Count 5 groups of five minutes to get 25 minutes.

Use the hour just passed, 5. Between midnight and 1 a.m. the hour is written 00.

The time is \(05:25\).

lessons.title: Elapsed time and crossing midnight
lessons.summary: Find durations and count forwards or backwards on a 24-hour clock.
lessons.objective: Find durations and count forwards or backwards on a 24-hour clock.
lessons.before: Recall how many minutes there are in one hour.
lessons.ideas:
Add the lengths of the jumps. Continue from 00:00 when crossing midnight.

Count forward. After 23:59 the next minute is 00:00 the next day.

Subtract the whole duration. Regroup one hour as 60 minutes when needed.
lessons.method:
How long passes between two readings?

Draw a timeline. Jump to the next whole hour, then onwards to the finish.

How can I find the finish time?

Start at the given time and add the duration. When the minute count reaches 60, make a new hour.

How can I find an earlier start time?

Start with the finish and count the duration backwards. If it helps, make jumps to a whole hour.
mistakes: The digits on a clock do not form a decimal number.
Count minutes on the clock in groups of 60.
Adding a duration to the finish tells you a later time.

examples.title: Count forward between two clock readings
examples.question: A session starts at \(23:20\) and finishes at \(00:08\) the next day. Give the duration in minutes.
examples.solution:
Count from \(23:20\) to \(00:00\): 40 minutes.

Then count 8 more minutes to \(00:08\). Add both jumps.

The answer is \(48\).

examples.title: Find the finish time
examples.question: An observation begins at \(22:15\) and lasts 27 minutes. Give its finish time in 24-hour notation.
examples.solution:
Convert \(22:15\) to 1335 minutes after midnight. Then add the 27 minutes.

Convert the result back to hours and minutes, moving to the next day if the result reaches 1440 minutes.

The time is \(22:42\).

examples.title: Find the start time
examples.question: A workshop must finish at \(23:16\). It lasts 29 minutes. Give its start time in 24-hour notation.
examples.solution:
Convert \(23:16\) to 1396 minutes after midnight. Then subtract the 29 minutes.

Convert the result back to hours and minutes, moving to the next day if the result reaches 1440 minutes.

The time is \(22:47\).

lessons.title: Timetables and time zones
lessons.summary: Read a timetable, choose a service and use a fixed local-time offset.
lessons.objective: Read a timetable, choose a service and use a fixed local-time offset.
lessons.before: Recall how many minutes there are in one hour.
lessons.ideas:
The same column shows all the times for one service.

Find the duration between the two times using jumps.

Add or subtract the offset. Change the day if your result crosses midnight.
lessons.method:
Which service arrives before the deadline?

Find the row for the destination, then pick the latest acceptable time. Follow that column back to the start.

How long does the journey take?

Read two times from the same service. Check which stop each time belongs to.

Which way does a local-time difference go?

When a place is ahead, its clock is later. When it is behind, its clock is earlier.
mistakes: A later departure is useful only if its arrival still meets the deadline.
Moving to another column chooses another service.
A local-time offset is a difference between clocks. A journey duration is a different quantity.

examples.title: Find the last service before a deadline
examples.question:
StopABC
Museum08:0408:2508:46
Square08:1908:4009:01
Library08:3008:5109:12

What is the latest departure time from the Museum that reaches the Library by \(08:52\)? Use 24-hour notation.
examples.solution:
Read along the Library row. Service C arrives after the deadline.

Follow the column for service B back to the Museum row.

The time is \(08:25\).

examples.title: Compare two times in one timetable column
examples.question:
StopABC
Museum08:0508:2708:49
Square08:2108:4309:05
Library08:3308:5509:17

How many minutes does service C take from the Museum to the Square?
examples.solution:
Read column C from \(08:49\) to \(09:05\).

Count the minutes between these times.

The answer is \(16\).

examples.title: Apply a fixed time-zone difference
examples.question: Town B is 210 minutes ahead of Town A. It is \(06:16\) in Town A. Find the local time in Town B, in 24-hour notation.
examples.solution:
Ahead of means add the time difference.

If the calculation crosses midnight, continue reading the other day's clock.

The time is \(09:46\).
